newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Bund vol paralysed as EMU plot thickens.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Bund vol paralysed as EMU plot thickens.

text.p: Confusion over over European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) has enmeshed Bund option volatility, leaving it trapped as volume withers, traders said on Wednesday.
"The volume of trade in mark products has dropped," said a broker at a major British brokerage on the LIFFE floor. "Sterling and Euroswiss products are lapping it up as a bolt-hole."
France threw EMU into confusion once again earlier this week when it said it needed time to study the stability pact -- an integral part of EU plans for a single currency.

A French government spokeswoman said on Wednesday there was a "positive atmosphere" in talks on Europe, and there was no divergence on European policy between President Chirac and Prime Minister Lionel Jospin.
But questions remain over whether a deal can be struck before the pact was due to be ratified at the Amsterdam summit next week.
Traders said there were so many different opinions on the likely outcome, from a stronger euro to bond market chaos, that many investors had just backed away from some markets completely.
Implied volatility of July serial options on the September Bund future on LIFFE was trading at 5.55 percent, down from 5.6 at the open.
August was unchanged at 5.4 percent, September was at 5.47 percent, down from 5.49 and December was 5.51 percent by 1000 GMT. September Bund futures were up 0.08 at 100.97.
"Usually, when trade is as quiet as this, volatility would come off," said a trader at a U.S. house. "But everyone's afraid of selling vol in case there's a big move in the underlying suddenly."
"But on the other hand, with nothing going on at the moment, there's no reason to buy it," he said.
Traders said there were few signs of volatility trades going through.

The biggest trade so far in the session was in the September series, where a European bank bought 1,200 September 97.00 strike puts. The volatility on that trade was 6.52 percent. Traders said the same house has consistently been in the market buying puts. -- Lisa Wilson, International Bonds Unit + 44 171 542 6137
